Maritime journalists under the auspices of the Network of Nigeria Maritime Journalists have announced that their conference will focus on the performance, policy direction and operational efficiency of the maritime industry under President Bola Tinubu’s administration. The group, in a statement jointly signed by its Chairman, Dele Aderibigbe, and Public Relations Officer, Jerry Aguigbo, said that the conference would also place particular emphasis on port modernisation, trade facilitation and revenue generation. The organisers added that the conference, billed for next week in Lagos, would bring together key policymakers, maritime regulators, industry leaders and other stakeholders to examine the future of Nigeria’s maritime sector. They disclosed that the conference would be chaired by a former Director-General of the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency, Temisan Omatseye, with the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, attending as Special Guest of Honour. Renowned maritime lawyer, Barrister Emeka Akabogu, SAN, will deliver the keynote address themed ‘Seaport Modernisation, Trade Facilitation and Revenue.’ Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Stakeholders call for forensic audit of NIMASA vessel funds APC credits Tinubu with N372bn student loans, education reforms Shipowners decry regulatory constraints stifling maritime devt “Key areas of discussion will include the modernisation of seaports and the renewal of critical infrastructure, improved trade facilitation, enhanced ease of doing business, revenue growth and measures to curb financial leakages,” the organisers stated. They added that participants would also examine opportunities for expanding the marine and blue economy, creating employment, strengthening maritime safety and security, and improving the overall competitiveness of Nigeria’s maritime sector. They stated that the gathering was expected to attract heads of government agencies, managing directors of shipping companies, terminal operators, freight forwarders and other prominent stakeholders across the maritime value chain. The organisers maintained that through the unity conference, NNMJ seeks to encourage informed dialogue, strengthen collaboration between public- and private-sector stakeholders, and promote policy initiatives that will enhance port efficiency, facilitate legitimate trade, improve revenue performance and unlock the economic potential of Nigeria’s maritime sector. “The conference is also expected to reinforce the role of the maritime media in promoting accountability, providing informed industry analysis and advancing constructive engagement on policies and reforms affecting the nation’s marine and blue economy,” it stated.
